battle.name: 484年嚈噠-薩珊戰爭
battle.brief: 公元484年，薩珊王佩羅茲傾國東征中亞，在阿姆河一線被嚈噠騎軍擊潰並遭生擒，繼而被迫以贖金、人質與割地議和。卡面的希臘重步兵本身不在此役，它點出的是方陣的成立條件：正面只在有展開空間時才結實，而484年的薩珊把方陣拖成了行軍縱隊，草原弓騎包抄兩翼，國王與盾牆一併淪陷。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 這場戰爭是薩珊波斯與嚈噠聯盟在中亞東北部的一場正面決戰，時間在公元484年。薩珊一方是伊朗高原的薩珊王朝，皇帝佩羅茲一世在位459至484年，是庫思老一世之子、巴赫拉姆五世之弟，484年時他正值壯年，卻沒有打過這種規模的仗。薩珊的國家機器以「國王之軍」（spāh）為核心：重騎大隊「庫林布」（korymbos，執矛重騎）與親軍「帕巴格」為骨幹，重甲騎兵披札甲與鎖子甲，衝鋒前先以弓箭覆蓋；步兵方面是「班德」式的密集重步兵大隊，由各封區與城鎮徵集，配大盾、長矛與鎖子甲，列成方陣；後勤靠王帳（divān）與驛站網，軍糧自美索不達米亞與呼羅珊的產糧區沿御道北運，鑄幣在泰西封、比沙普爾等地進行。邊疆上，薩珊的實際控制線沿阿姆河上游與興都庫什山北麓的花剌子模、索格底亞、巴克特里亞（吐火羅）一線，防守靠封區邊將（marzban）與地方貴族，力量有限。嚈噠一方是游牧部族聯盟，骨幹是源自匈奴的嚈噠本族，中文古籍或稱白匈奴，《魏書》與《北史·西域傳》把他們列為高車的一支，住在蔥嶺以西；最高統帥是可汗，下轄數支部族聯盟，核心是草原騎兵：複合反曲弓的弓騎、披札甲與骨片綴成鱗甲的輕騎、帶長矛的衝鋒重騎。中國正史形容其「控弦數十萬」，屬於概數，實際編制遠少於此，但足以在任何一段邊境上壓過薩珊的徵召兵。嚈噠的實力還橫跨兩條戰線：484年他們同時在印度河上游與笈多王朝交兵，在高加索方向威脅羅馬的亞美尼亞與卡帕多細亞邊境，而薩珊的另一端正被羅馬與叛位的卡瓦德牽制。戰爭的勝負，就在這樣兩面受敵的處境下，由佩羅茲的一次冒險決定。
countriesEn: This war was a set-piece collision between the Sasanian Empire and the Hephthalite confederation in the far north-east of Central Asia, fought in 484 AD. The Sasanian side was the Iranian plateau empire of the Sasanian dynasty, ruled by the shah Peroz I, who reigned from 459 to 484, son of Khosrow I and brother of Bahram V. In 484 he was in the prime of his life but had never fought a war on this scale. The Sasanian state machine was organised around the king's army, the spah: the backbone was the heavy cavalry, the korymbos of spear-bearing riders and the royal guard corps of the Papak, armoured riders in lamellar and mail fighting with long lances, their charge preceded by a screen of archers. On the infantry side stood the massed heavy foot of the paband, levied from the provinces and the towns, with large shields, spears and mail, drawn up in a phalanx. Logistically the host depended on the royal camp, the divan, and on a relay of posting stations, with grain moving north from the food-producing districts of Mesopotamia and Khorasan along the royal road, and the coinage struck at Ctesiphon, Bishapur and other mints. On the frontier the effective Sasanian line ran along the upper Amu Darya and the northern foot of the Hindu Kush, across Khwarezm, Sogdia and Bactria in Tokharistan, and it was held by provincial marquesses and local nobles whose forces were thin and unhardened. The other side was a nomadic tribal confederation whose core was the Hephthalites themselves, descended from the Xiongnu and called the White Huns in the Chinese books, which the Wei Shu and the chapter on the Western Regions in the Bei Shi list as a branch of the Gaoche living west of the Pamirs. At the head stood a khan ruling a number of tribal groups, with the grassland horse as the backbone: riders with composite recurved bows, light horse in lamellar and bone-plate armour, and lancers for the charge. The Chinese official histories describe their bowmen in round figures of tens of thousands; the real establishment was far smaller, but it was enough to outweigh the Sasanian levies on any stretch of frontier. The Hephthalite strength also straddled two fronts: in 484 they were fighting the Gupta Empire on the upper Indus, they were pressing Roman Armenia and Cappadocia in the Caucasus direction, and at the other end the Sasanian state was pinned by Rome and by the rebel Kavad. The war was decided, in that two-sided pressure, by one gamble made by Peroz.
people: 佩羅茲一世是這場戰爭的失敗主角。他是薩珊王朝第一位在戰場上被敵軍生擒的君主，事後的阿拉伯與波斯史家對他的評價極不客氣，說他輕舉妄動、不聽勸告，執意親征。記錄此役的史料分成兩層：底層是薩珊的《胡達伊納馬格》（Khwaday-Namag）殘篇，經中世紀的阿拉伯史家轉述而保存下來；上層是九世紀的塔巴里、雅庫比，十世紀的拜拉米，以及菲爾多西《史詩王書》中佩羅茲一世那一篇。嚈噠方面的主帥姓名沒有可靠記載：較晚的阿拉伯敘事把這位可汗稱為阿克什溫瓦爾（Akhshunwar），六世紀的阿拉伯詩作中又見托拉之名，學界多認為是同名異譯或後人附會，無法確定。真正留下姓名的，是薩珊一方的北境將領與被擄的使節：傳記說佩羅茲被擒後，嚈噠可汗派人與他談判，約定贖金、人質與割地；第二次敗後，波斯一方又派出一名年老的僧侶作中間人，徒步走到可汗營前求見，才換得放人。佩羅茲回到國都之後，在位僅數月便於484至485年間戰死，據說是追擊北方的匈奴部眾時中伏身亡，後世為他立廟，配享的規格被削到極低，葬禮草草。次子小佩羅茲（484至493年）接位後延續對嚈噠的戰爭，493年死於北方部族之手；叔父巴萊什在交接期內曾短暫即位。中國方面的旁證來自正史：《北史·西域傳》記于闐曾上表請魏朝出兵討嚈噠而未獲批准，說明當時中亞的局勢已牽動到中國西北的邊策；史家同時記下嚈噠與波斯互通的使者往來，可見薩珊王朝的敗訊在當時已傳到蔥嶺以東。
peopleEn: Peroz I is the loser at the centre of this war. He was the first Sasanian monarch ever taken alive on the field, and the later Arab and Persian historians are merciless about him, saying that he was rash, that he took bad advice, and that he insisted on leading the campaign in person. The record of the war comes in two layers. The lower layer is the surviving fragments of the Sasanian Khwaday-Namag, preserved through the mediation of medieval Arab historians. The upper layer is the ninth-century al-Tabari and al-Yaqubi, the tenth-century Bal'ami, and the section on Peroz I in Firdausi's Shahnameh. The name of the Hephthalite commander is not reliably recorded: later Arab narrative calls this khan Akhshunwar, and the name Tora appears in sixth-century Arabic poetry; scholars generally treat these as variant transliterations of one name or as later invention, and nothing can be settled. The names that do survive are on the Persian side, in the frontier commanders and in the envoys: the tradition says that after Peroz was captured, the Hephthalite khan sent men to treat with him, and that ransom, hostages and territory were the terms discussed; after the second defeat the Persians sent out an old man of the faith, a monk, who walked to the khan's camp and was admitted, and only his intercession bought the king's release. Peroz returned to the capital, but he held the throne for only a few months before he was killed in 484 or 485, reportedly cut down in an ambush while pursuing Hunnic tribes in the north; the temple later raised to him was given a very shabby allotment of worship, and his burial was perfunctory. His younger son, Peroz II, who reigned from 484 to 493, carried on the war against the Hephthalites and was killed by northern tribes in 493; his uncle Balash briefly took the throne during the handover. The Chinese evidence is a side echo: the chapter on the Western Regions in the Bei Shi records that Khotan petitioned the Northern Wei for troops against the Hephthalites and was refused, which shows how far the instability of Central Asia already reached into Chinese frontier policy; the same histories record the exchange of envoys between the Hephthalites and Persia, so the news of the Sasanian defeat had already travelled east of the Pamirs.
kits: 卡面這件希臘重步兵（hoplite）是公元前五世紀的裝備：圓形盾牌、青銅頭盔、青銅胸甲與護肩、短劍（xiphos），以及兩米多長的長矛（dory）。到公元484年，這一整套已退場近千年，卡面件本身不在此役現場；它真正延續下來的不是形制而是原理——密集的方陣，盾牌互相遮蔽，個人靠隊形而不是靠個人武藝活命，而方陣的正面只在有展開空間時才真正結實。亞歷山大東征之後，希臘式重裝步兵的方陣傳入伊朗，薩珊王朝把它改造成自己的「班德」重步兵大隊：大盾、長矛、札甲與鎖子甲密集排列，正面極難撬動；六世紀的拜占庭史家普羅科匹烏斯描述薩珊軍陣時，仍直接拿它與希臘方陣相比，說兩者的密集程度與正面抗衝擊力相近。所以這張卡在戰役中的位置，是薩珊大軍裡最硬的那一段：佩羅茲把大量徵召的步兵排成方陣，企圖以盾牆擋住草原騎兵。事實證明這一段正是薩珊的弱點——密集成方陣的步兵在開闊地上正對大量弓騎時沒有還手之力，盾牌擋得住箭矢，擋不住包抄。與之對比的是嚈噠的裝備體系：反曲複合弓配重箭，札甲與骨片綴成的鱗甲，配鞍具的草原馬，彎刀與長矛，五世紀後期才開始在草原裝備中出現的馬鐙，以及為持久戰備下的馬匹與乳酪食糧。薩珊的重騎同樣精良，騎兵用札甲長衫覆馬，長矛夾在腋下衝鋒，背負圓盾，但重甲騎兵在鬆軟的河谷地形上轉向遲緩，一旦被大量弓騎包圍就發揮不出衝撞力。攻城方面，薩珊遠征軍帶著塔與投石器械行軍，圍攻堡壘時靠寨牆與投射武器抵禦；全軍的凝聚點是薩珊的制式旗幟「登克」（Dēnk，露兜樹紋錦旗），這面旗幟並未在此役失落，它是在530年的薩塔拉之役落入拜占庭將軍貝利撒留之手，並被保存在君士坦丁堡。
kitsEn: The Greek hoplite on the card dates from the fifth century BC: a round shield, a bronze helmet, a bronze cuirass and shoulder guards, a short sword, the xiphos, and a spear more than two metres long, the dory. By 484 AD the whole set had been out of use for nearly a millennium. What actually survived was not the form but the principle: a dense phalanx in which shields shelter one another, where the individual lives by the formation rather than by his own prowess. After Alexander's conquests the Greek heavy infantry phalanx reached Iran, and the Sasanian dynasty recast it as its own paband of heavy infantry, large shields, spears, lamellar and mail, packed close enough to be very hard to prise open. When Procopius describes Sasanian formations in the sixth century he still compares them directly with the Greek phalanx, saying that their density and their resistance to a frontal shock are comparable. So the card's place in the battle is the hardest segment of the whole Sasanian host: Peroz drew up the mass of his levied infantry in a phalanx, hoping to hold the grassland horse with a wall of shields. In the event that segment was exactly the Persian weakness, because compact infantry in the open, facing massed mounted archers, has no answer: a shield stops arrows, it does not stop encirclement. Set against it stands the Hephthalite equipment system: composite recurved bows with heavy arrows, lamellar and bone-plate armour, grassland horses with their own tack, sabres and lances, the stirrup only beginning to appear in steppe equipment in the late fifth century, and the horse herds and dairy provisions that made a long campaign possible. The Sasanian heavy cavalry was no less well equipped, riders and horses covered by long lamellar barding, the lance couched under the arm, a round shield on the back, but armoured horse turns slowly in soft river-bottom ground, and once surrounded by massed archers the charge has nothing left to spend. On the siege side the marching column carried towers and stone-throwers, and when it sat down before a fortress it relied on the palisade and on missile troops for its defence. The rallying point of the whole army was the Sasanian standard, the Denk with its tree-of-life design in silk; that banner did not fall here, it was captured by Belisarius at Satala in 530 and kept in Constantinople.
tactics: 這場戰役的戰術主軸，是草原式騎射與希臘式方陣的正面碰撞。嚈噠人先把大量輕騎散開在兩翼與側後，以反曲弓覆蓋波斯軍的縱隊，正面只留少量重騎與步兵；一旦波斯軍主力壓上，就反覆做出假退——一邊後撤一邊用箭雨覆蓋追兵——把薩珊的前鋒與本隊拉成一條細長的縱隊，迫使其在狹窄的河谷或隘道中疊成密不可分的隊形，無法展開成方陣的寬面。等薩珊的縱隊被拉長、指揮中樞與後方輜重暴露在平地上，嚈噠的重騎即由兩翼合攏完成包抄，同時以正面弓騎的箭雨壓制，使被包住的步兵抬不起身。此役最關鍵的一擊不是硬衝，而是把對方從「有寬度的方陣」變成「沒有寬度的縱隊」：hoplite 式的盾牆一旦失去展開的空間，就只剩盾牌朝外的一堵牆。第二次交鋒，嚈噠人不再急於決戰，而是把波斯軍圍困在一處堡壘與營寨之間，以弓騎輪番襲擾、封鎖道路，切斷其樵採與牧放，等援軍與糧秣耗盡，再以優厚條件誘使國王本人前來議和。薩珊一方在這一階段也做了能做的努力：守方依托寨牆以投射武器與弓弩消耗敵騎，並嘗試以小股騎兵夜襲營壘；但薩珊遠征軍的機動全靠馬匹與大量轎馬輜重，離開水源與牧場就寸步難行，兩次遠征都敗在補給線，而不是敗在正面。
tacticsEn: The tactical hinge of the battle is the collision between steppe mounted archery and the Greek phalanx. The Hephthalites first spread large numbers of light horse on the flanks and the rear, covering the Persian columns with recurved bows and keeping only a little heavy cavalry and foot in front. As soon as the main weight of the Persian army pressed forward, they repeated the feigned retreat, drawing back while showering the pursuers with arrows, pulling the Persian vanguard and the army's centre into a thin, drawn-out column, forcing it to pile up in a narrow valley or defile where it could not deploy to the width of a phalanx. Once the column was stretched, with the command centre and the baggage exposed on open ground, the Hephthalite heavy horse closed in from both wings to complete the encirclement, while the mounted archers in front kept the trapped infantry pinned under arrow fire. The decisive stroke of this battle was not a charge but a transformation: the enemy was turned from a phalanx with breadth into a column without it. A hoplite wall of shields, once it loses the room to deploy, is only a wall with its shields facing outward. In the second phase the Hephthalites were in no hurry to give decisive battle: they shut the Persian army in between a fortress and its own camp, harried it with successive waves of mounted archers and cut the roads, so that firewood, forage and relief were denied, and then waited for the supplies of the besieged to run out before offering generous terms to draw the king himself into a meeting. The Persians did what they could in that phase: the defenders used the palisade and missile troops, including bolts, to wear down the enemy horse, and tried night raids on the Hephthalite camp with small bodies of horse. But the mobility of the Sasanian column rested entirely on its horses and its long train of baggage animals; away from water and pasture it could not move, and both of Peroz's campaigns were lost on the supply line rather than in the front line.
data: 關於這場戰爭，傳世數字極少，可核對的主要是年代、地理與制度三類。年代線清楚：佩羅茲一世在位459至484年，484年兵敗被擒，同年或次年死於北方戰事；小佩羅茲484至493年在位，493年陣亡；卡瓦德一世484年末第二度即位，嚈噠的壓力直到查士丁一世在位的567年才被逐出索格底亞。地理上，戰場在中亞東北部，傳記稱在「札普」（Zap）河一線，學者有考訂為阿姆河上游者，也有指錫爾河上游札卜河或瓦克什河支流者，說法不一，本卡經緯度取阿姆河上游一線。薩珊軍的出征路線自呼羅珊的木鹿、巴克赫與撒馬爾罕方向北上，越過索格底亞盆地的灌溉綠洲，進入嚈噠控制下的吐火羅與巴克特里亞，行程以千公里計，途中水源與牧場就是生死線。兵力方面，阿拉伯與波斯史家只給概數：常見說法是薩珊軍為數十萬之眾，並有北方匈奴部眾以大量騎兵來助；中國正史形容嚈噠「控弦數十萬」，同樣是概數，實際當遠少於此。可比的硬數字在財政上：薩珊王室的年收入與鑄幣量，遠不足以同時維持一支遠征軍與一筆對外賠款，這正是談判桌上波斯全面讓步的底牌；軍用道路由驛站組成，補給車隊的載量決定遠征軍的推進速度。損失沒有可信數字，只知第一次敗後波斯軍被大量俘虜與散失，王帳財貨盡為敵所得；贖金與歲貢的金額，傳記以「萬計」形容，顯係誇大，但足以說明數量級已超出波斯國庫的常規支出。第二次圍困延續了數月，時間的消耗本身就是勝因；戰役的確切月份史無明載，按中亞的行軍與牧場季節推算，最可能落在春末夏初。卡面那件公元前五世紀的希臘重步兵並不在此役的戰場上：現場只有它的原理，以薩珊「班德」重步兵的樣子延續下來。
dataEn: Few figures survive for this war, and what can be checked falls into three kinds: chronology, geography and institutions. The chronology is clear. Peroz I reigned from 459 to 484, was beaten and captured in 484, and died in a northern war in 484 or 485; Peroz II reigned from 484 to 493 and fell in 493; Kavad I took the throne again at the end of 484, and the Hephthalite pressure on Sogdia was not thrown off until 567, in the reign of Khosrow I. On geography, the battlefield lay in the far north-east of Central Asia, in the tradition at the river the sources call the Zap; scholars have identified it variously with the upper Amu Darya, with the Zhab in the upper Syr Darya, and with a tributary of the Vakhsh, and the coordinates here follow the upper Amu Darya. The marching route of the Persian column ran north from Merv, Balkh and Samarkand in Khorasan, across the irrigated oases of the Sogdian basin, into Tokharistan and Bactria under Hephthalite control, a distance counted in thousands of kilometres, along a line where water and pasture were the difference between living and perishing. On numbers of men, the Arab and Persian historians give only round figures: the usual statement is that the Sasanian host numbered tens of thousands of tens, and that Hunnic tribes from the north joined with a large body of horse; the Chinese official histories likewise speak of the Hephthalites with tens of thousands of bowmen, again a round figure, and the real establishment was far smaller. The hard numbers that do exist are fiscal. The annual revenue of the Sasanian court and its output of coinage could not easily support a far-flung campaign and a war indemnity at the same time, and that was the card Persia played when it gave way at the negotiating table. The military road system was a chain of posting stations, and the carrying capacity of the supply convoy set the speed of the whole column. There is no credible figure for the losses; all that is known is that after the first defeat a large part of the Persian army was taken or scattered and that the royal camp with its treasure fell to the enemy. The ransom and the annual tribute are described in round figures of tens of thousands, plainly exaggerated, but enough to show that the order of magnitude lay beyond the normal spending of the Persian treasury. The second blockade lasted months, and the consumption of time was itself the cause of victory. The exact month of the fighting is not recorded; judged by the campaigning and grazing seasons of Central Asia it most likely fell in late spring or early summer. The hoplite on the card was not on this battlefield: only its principle was, in the shape of the Sasanian paband of heavy infantry.
cause: 打起來有三層原因。最遠的一層是邊疆結構：四世紀末以後，嚈噠聯盟受魯然與突厥的向西壓力所迫，遷入吐火羅、巴克特里亞與花剌子模一帶，牧場與戰利品的空間被壓縮，必然向南、向西擴張；而薩珊在東北亞的實際控制只到索格底亞與花剌子模的綠洲城市，邊防靠封區貴族與地方民兵，鬆散而少經大戰。第二層是薩珊自己的前科：450年前後亞美尼亞的佩羅茲起兵反抗薩珊，兵敗後逃到嚈噠那裡求助，隨即被嚈噠人殺死，薩珊為此付出沉重代價；此後嚈噠每有南下，薩珊的東北邊境就多付一次錢，五世紀中葉卡瓦德一世還曾靠嚈噠的兵馬奪位並向他們支付巨款，這在薩珊宮廷是難堪的記憶。第三層是484年的時機判斷：嚈噠正在印度河上游與笈多王朝交兵，又在高加索方向威脅羅馬邊境，薩珊以為找到了對方分兵的空隙；佩羅茲集結東境與呼羅珊的全部可用兵力傾國東征，志在一次解決。然而他的判斷建立在薩珊自己的經驗上——密集的步兵方陣與重騎大隊足以正面壓垮草原騎兵，這是薩珊的傳統所教的；問題在於方陣離開了御道與水源就沒有展開的空間，而草原騎兵從來不給他這個空間。兩軍在阿姆河一線相遇時，佩羅茲的計劃已經在行軍途中被地形悄悄改寫。
causeEn: There are three layers of cause. The furthest back is the structure of the frontier. From the late fourth century the Hephthalite confederation, pushed west by the Rouran and the Turks, moved into Tokharistan, Bactria and Khwarezm, where the room for pasture and for plunder was compressed, so that expansion south and west became unavoidable. The effective Sasanian control in the north-east reached only to the oasis cities of Sogdia and Khwarezm, and the border was held by provincial nobles and local militia, loose and unhardened by war. The second layer is Persia's own record. Around 450 the Armenian Peroz rose against the Sasanians, was defeated, fled to the Hephthalites for help and was then killed by them, and Sasanian Persia paid dearly for that. Ever afterwards every Hephthalite move southward cost the Sasanian north-east another payment; in the middle of the fifth century Kavad I even took the throne with Hephthalite soldiers and paid them a large sum, and that was a humiliating memory in the Sasanian court. The third layer is the reading of the moment in 484. The Hephthalites were engaged with the Guptas on the upper Indus and at the same time threatening the Roman frontier across the Caucasus, and Persia thought it had found a gap in their attention. Peroz gathered every available man from the eastern provinces and from Khorasan and marched east with the whole nation, meaning to settle the matter in one stroke. But his reading rested on Persian experience: a dense infantry phalanx and a heavy cavalry could crush grassland horse head on, as Sasanian tradition taught. The trouble was that a phalanx away from the royal road and from water has no room to deploy, and the grassland horsemen were never going to give him that room. By the time the two armies met on the line of the Amu Darya, Peroz's plan had already been quietly rewritten by the terrain on the march.
impact: 這場敗仗對薩珊的傷害，遠大於戰場上的損失本身。首先是王室的威信：佩羅茲一世是薩珊第一位被敵軍生擒的皇帝，他的被俘被記成王朝的國恥，民間與宮廷的敘事把「國王在陣前被捉走」寫成一則永恆的教訓，菲爾多西在《史詩王書》中特別把佩羅茲的失敗寫成輕率與傲慢的懲罰。其次是國土與財政：薩珊被迫割讓索格底亞與花剌子模一帶的權益，支付一次性贖金與歲貢，並以王子與公主作人質，東北邊防實際上由對方掌控，這等於把中亞商路的保護費交到嚈噠手上；遠征軍的消耗又讓本已吃緊的國庫更形枯竭，五世紀末的薩珊鑄幣因此漸見輕重不一。第三是戰略上的連鎖反應：484年嚈噠在東線重創薩珊，行動力隨即轉向西方，同年他們就打到羅馬的卡帕多細亞與亞美尼亞邊境，在蘇赫拉與羅馬軍交鋒；羅馬皇帝澤諾在484年1月倒台，新登基的阿納斯塔修一世選擇用錢買和平，向嚈噠支付重金換取邊境安寧，而薩珊正是靠這段西線的鬆動才沒有同時被兩面夾擊。第四是更長期的秩序變化：嚈噠聯盟在484年達到頂點，其騎兵隨後深入印度河上游，擊敗笈多王朝的斯坎德笈多，在西北印度建立以白匈奴為名的政權；中亞則出現權力真空，北方部族（後來被阿拉伯史家稱為匈奴，一般認為與突厥系相關）趁勢南下，終於在493年殺死小佩羅茲，使薩珊的東北戰線再亂十年，直到查士丁一世於567年才把嚈噠人逐出索格底亞，收回河中地區的門戶。對薩珊而言，484年不是一場戰役的失敗，而是東北邊防被連續撬開半個世紀的起點。
impactEn: The damage this defeat did to Persia was far greater than the losses on the field. First came the prestige of the crown. Peroz I was the first Sasanian shah ever taken alive by an enemy, and his captivity was written up as a national disgrace; the narrative tradition, in the court and in the country, turned the king dragged off the front line into a permanent lesson, and Firdausi in the Shahnameh made the defeat of Peroz the punishment of his own rashness and arrogance. Second came territory and money. Persia was forced to concede its interests in Sogdia and Khwarezm, to pay a lump-sum ransom and an annual tribute, and to leave a prince and a princess as hostages; the north-eastern frontier passed in practice into the hands of the other side, which is to say that the protection money of the Central Asian trade routes went to the Hephthalites. The cost of the campaign drained an already tight treasury, and the Sasanian coinage of the late fifth century grew visibly irregular in weight. Third came the chain reaction in strategy. Having crushed Persia in the east in 484, the Hephthalites turned their whole strength westwards and struck Roman Cappadocia and Armenia in the same year, meeting the Roman army at Satala; the Roman emperor Zeno was overthrown in the Nika riots of January 484, and the new emperor Anastasius I chose to buy peace with money, paying the Hephthalites heavily for frontier quiet, while the loosening of that western front was exactly what kept Persia from being attacked on two sides at once. Fourth came the longer reordering of the region. The Hephthalite confederation reached its height in 484, its horse riding deep into the upper Indus, defeating Skandagupta of the Gupta realm and setting up a polity of the White Huns in north-western India; a vacuum opened in Central Asia, and northern tribes, called Huns by the Arab historians and generally linked to the Turkic peoples, moved south, finally killing Peroz II in 493 and throwing the Sasanian north-eastern front into disorder for another ten years, until Khosrow I in 567 finally drove the Hephthalites out of Sogdia and recovered the approaches to the lands between the rivers. For Persia, 484 was not the loss of a battle but the opening of half a century in which the north-eastern frontier was prised open again and again.
result: 結局是清楚的：薩珊敗。佩羅茲的大軍在阿姆河一線崩潰，他本人在亂軍中被生擒，王帳、財貨與大部分輜重盡為嚈噠所得，這在薩珊的歷史上是沒有先例的。嚈噠可汗沒有趕盡殺絕，而是先以巨額贖金、人質與割地為條件放人，佩羅茲回到國都；隨即他再集兵反攻，第二次又在堡壘與圍困中失敗，兵力和補給耗盡，最後在對方提出的條件下議和：薩珊承認以定期歲貢換取和平，割讓索格底亞的權益，並把王子與公主留在嚈噠王室作人質。佩羅茲本人沒有等到復國，他在484至485年間率軍追擊北方的匈奴部眾時戰死，廟號與祭祀規格被大幅削減，葬禮草草。繼位的小佩羅茲（484至493年）延續同一條戰線，卻再未取勝，493年死於北方部族的刀下；王位回到卡瓦德一世手中，局勢才勉強穩定，東北邊境又打了半個世紀，直到567年才由薩珊收復索格底亞。戰役的直接成果因此是：嚈噠拿到了中亞東部的霸權、薩珊的歲貢與人質，以及一位在陣前被俘的薩珊皇帝；它的長期成果則是延後數十年才兌現——薩珊王朝最終在東線把嚈噠逐出河中，靠的是比佩羅茲更長的耐性與查士丁一世的改革，而不是任何一場方陣的奇蹟。
resultEn: The outcome is clear: Persia lost. Peroz's army collapsed on the line of the Amu Darya, he was taken alive in the rout, and the royal camp with its treasure and most of the baggage fell to the Hephthalites, something without precedent in Sasanian history. The Hephthalite khan did not finish the business. He released the king first, on terms of a large ransom, hostages and territory, and Peroz went back to his capital. Then Peroz mustered another army and marched against them again, and was beaten a second time, this time shut up between fortress and camp with his supplies and strength exhausted, and peace was made on the terms the other side dictated: the Sasanians recognised an annual tribute in return for quiet, conceded their interests in Sogdia, and left a prince and a princess in the Hephthalite royal house as hostages. Peroz himself never got to rebuild his position. In 484 or 485 he was killed while pursuing Hunnic tribes in the north, his cult foundation and his share of worship cut back hard and his burial hurried. His successor Peroz II, reigning from 484 to 493, carried on the same front and never won, dying in 493 under the knife of northern tribes; the throne came back to Kavad I, the situation stabilised only in part, and the north-eastern frontier fought on for half a century more until Persia recovered Sogdia in 567. The immediate results of the war are therefore these: the Hephthalites gained the hegemony of eastern Central Asia, the Sasanian tribute and the Sasanian hostages, and a Sasanian king taken alive on the front line. The long-term result was deferred by decades, and the dynasty that finally drove the Hephthalites out of the lands between the rivers did it with a patience Peroz did not have and with the reforms of Khosrow I, not with the miracle of any phalanx.
